original_question: Is the following problem decidable, and if so, what is its complexity? Given a finite group G, is there a finite group H such that the derived subgroup of H is isomorphic to G?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.32 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)", posed by P. J. Cameron.
correct_elements: Your draft is essentially the paper's exact target. It correctly asks about a decision problem on a finite input group G, asks for the existence of a finite witness group H, uses the right structural condition that the derived subgroup of H be isomorphic to G, and keeps the paper's algorithmic emphasis on decidability and complexity.
missing_details: To make the question fully self-contained, it helps to spell out that the derived subgroup means the commutator subgroup H' = [H,H].

A formal complexity question requires a specified encoding/presentation of the input finite group G (for example, Cayley table, permutation group, matrix group, or finite presentation); the paper does not fix this, so any precise complexity claim must state the input model.
It is implicit that the problem is a yes/no decision problem asking only for existence of such an H, not for classification of all such H or for an explicit construction.
refined_question: After fixing a standard encoding of finite groups as input, determine whether the following decision problem is decidable and, if it is, determine its computational complexity: given a finite group G, does there exist a finite group H whose derived (commutator) subgroup H' = [H,H] is abstractly isomorphic to G?
justification: The draft matches Problem 21.32 almost verbatim, so the faithful refinement is not to broaden it but only to make its standard notation explicit and to surface the one computational detail the Kourovka formulation leaves implicit, namely the representation of the input finite group. There is no nearby theorem, proposition, or paper-internal reformulation attached to this problem in the cited location, so the sharpest stand-alone version is the same existence question for finite commutator subgroups, stated as a decision problem with an explicit input model.
